utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case number IT-02-61-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference to review the progress on procedural matters. May I have the parties, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon, representing the Office of the Prosecutor. Appearing with me to my right is Ms. Camille Bibles, to her right, Mr. Mark Vlasic; and to his right, the case manager, Mr. David Bruff. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am the Defence counsel for the accused, Miroslav Deronjic. My name is Slobodan Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to find out from the accused whether he can hear the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, yes, I can follow. Everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Yes. I think I'll start with the Prosecution to find out on disclosure issues, Rule 66(A)(i). Any progress?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have disclosed to the Defence all of the materials under 66(A)(i), and in respect of 66(A)(ii), we have disclosed the majority of witness statements to the accused. We have conducted additional interviews. A mission was just completed in November. We have two additional statements that we are reviewing, and we will be disclosing to the Defence very, very shortly. In addition to that, there are matters relating to Rule 68, although they may have been previously disclosed, our record-keeping on that is incomplete and we will be redisclosing the two documents relating to Rule 68 to the Defence very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. From what the Prosecution have said, that they have conducted interviews and there are two more statements, witness statements, to be produced to the Defence, does that mean that the Prosecution more or less are decided on the number of witnesses they -- potential witnesses for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence, is what the Prosecution have said in accordance with your record so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just received the answer to the question that I was planning to put during the Status Conference; namely, after the first Status Conference, I think even on the same day, I received the material that Mr. Harmon has talked about, and then after -- and after I received this initial material under Rule 66, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there was a gap of four months, during which I didn't receive anything. But then today, for the first time, I'm hearing that there is something else, and I was planning to ask whether there was anything more to be disclosed, because it was rather unusual not to receive anything during the past four months. So I have just received an answer on that question, so there is no need for me to discuss that any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. If that is the status on disclosure and what the Prosecution -- the ongoing obligation under Rule 68, then it means that we are closer to the next step in the proceedings, giving due time to the Defence for the latest statements that have been -- or that are going to be disclosed to them. So can we say that we are more or less up to date, except for the next big process?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I would like to ask the accused: Is there anything about your conditions of detention that you'd like the Trial Chamber to know? Is everything all right: Your health, food, the conditions under which you are being looked after? Is everything all right with you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I don't have any remarks relating to my accommodation. My health is not the best, but that's very well. Basically, everything is all right. And like I said at the previous Status Conference, I don't have anything to remark on regarding my accommodation or detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You may be seated. Is there anything else any of the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There's nothing on behalf of the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Defence? Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has nothing at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then our Status Conference has been -- is short, because it appears to me that there is compliance of the procedural rules. There being nothing else to discuss, then we'll close the Status Conference until next time. The court will rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at.
